newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back to end mixed, NY slips.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back to end mixed, NY slips.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures pulled back from early highs to end Monday tightly mixed as New York took a tumble despite news of a sharp draw in U.S. green coffee stocks.
Traders said by the close, benchmark January contract was $5 higher at $1,447 a tonne after fluctuating within a $23 range.
"London is more or less unchanged, it has not done anything since making its due of $10 higher," said one. "It's very difficult to second guess where the market should be going."
Volume was an unimpressive 2,359 lots, centred mainly on the January contract.
Traders said the market rose early on light fund buying in anticipation of further New York gains on the back of a sharp fall in the Green Coffee Association's (GCA) October stock figures.
New York started higher on shortcovering on the GCA numbers.
But the market soon retreated, pounded by producer hedge selling and local long liquidation ahead of December's first notice day, traders said.
The GCA said on Friday that green coffee supplies in U.S. warehouses fell by 351,600 60-kg bags to 1.26 million bags, the lowest level since the GCA began tracking data in 1988.
The market had expected the data to show a decline of between 200,000 and 300,000 bags.

But some traders reckoned that, based on the buying activity in the run-up to the report, the news could have been priced into the market. New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) certified stock data are due after the close of trading on Monday.
A modest 1,250 bags of coffee were pending grading by the exchange as of last week and traders were keeping a close watch to see if the pendings showed a significant improvement.
Tuesday is the first notice day for CSCE's December contract. December's open interest is around 4,461 lots as of November 14 but certified stocks are virtually nil.
In the physical sector, traders said Ugandan coffee arrivals were reported to be good but Zairean supplies had been reduced to a trickle due to the country's political crisis.

Tanzania's domestic coffee prices have risen on good demand by international buyers, one trader said, while Vietnamese origins were said to be having difficulty getting certification due to high moisture content.
